subject: maths
question: In what duration will a sum of money double itself at 10% per annum rate of simple interest?
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = Amount (A) / 2 (as the sum doubles itself)

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = ?

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

When the sum doubles, Amount (A) = Principal (P) + SI

⇒ SI = P

**Calculation:**

SI = P

⇒ P = (P × R × T) / 100

⇒ 1 = (R × T) / 100

⇒ T = 100 / R

⇒ T = 100 / 10

⇒ T = 10 years

**∴ The sum of money will double itself in 10 years.**
